clue.text: Factory worker ready to supply remote control device

blocks.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in a factory hand
set means prepared, as in 'ready, steady, go'

explanation.surface: A factory hand stands ready to hand over a remote control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Factory worker' reads as one person, but the worker alone is the first piece; 'factory' only colours the noun, as in 'farm hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: A handset is the handheld unit used to operate a television or similar appliance from across the room.

clue.text: Something that might be blown in the presence of English writer

blocks.note: a horn is an instrument or signal that is blown
standing by someone is being in their presence

explanation.surface: Something gets blown while an English author looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick HORNBY is the English novelist of Fever Pitch and High Fidelity.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Hornby is a well-known contemporary novelist born in England, so he is an example of the category named.

clue.text: New item required for archery is restricted

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
archers shoot arrows

explanation.surface: A new piece of archery equipment is in short supply.
explanation.walkthrough: N for new is a standard abbreviation, attached to the front of the archery item.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow and restricted both describe something limited in scope or range, a straightforward synonym pairing.

clue.text: Regard for number one?

blocks.note: surface reading: respect for whoever is in first place, the leader or champion
setter's reading: 'number one' is slang for oneself, so this is regard for yourself

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' suggests a winner or a chart-topper, but the idiom 'looking after number one' means looking after yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-esteem is the respect or good opinion a person holds of themselves, which is regard aimed at your own person.

clue.text: Knob in brass instrument mentioned

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken about, so we want a word heard rather than read

blocks.note: the tuba is the big bass brass instrument; in a non-rhotic accent the two words sound alike

explanation.surface: A dial or knob on a brass instrument gets a mention.
explanation.walkthrough: The match relies on a British accent where the final R is not pronounced, so TUBA and TUBER are said identically.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuber is a swollen rounded growth on a root or stem, like a potato, so a knob in the sense of a lump.

clue.text: A cop is excited about southern artist

indicators.note: excited things are agitated and jumbled, so these letters get stirred up
about means surrounding, so one part goes round another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A police officer gets worked up about a painter from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does double duty in the surface but here it is part of the letters to rearrange; the six letters go round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism, an obvious example of a great artist.

clue.text: Fine type of pottery is evident around sides of older church

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word wraps the others
the sides of a word are its two outer edges, its first and last letters

blocks.note: plain means obvious or evident
the first and last letters of the word
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Fine pottery is on show around the edges of an old church.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAIN splits after its first letter to hold OR and CE: P-ORCE-LAIN. CE for Church of England is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is a hard, white, translucent ceramic, the finest kind of china made by potters.

clue.text: Companion has a time for casual conversation

blocks.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
'has' just joins; the A is taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A friend makes time for a relaxed natter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Companion of Honour is a British award whose holders put CH after their names.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal talk between people, the plain meaning of relaxed conversation.

clue.text: Songwriter is honed after working on first of musicals

indicators.note: working means being set in motion and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged
the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A songwriter's craft is sharpened by working on musicals.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' places the reshuffled letters above the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Sondheim wrote the music and lyrics for Company and Sweeney Todd, making him a celebrated composer of songs.

clue.text: Utter slogan of a leftist?

blocks.note: first meaning: complete, total, as in an utter disaster
second meaning, punning: someone on the left would chant for the political right to be out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like a verb, to speak, but it is the adjective meaning complete; the second part splits the answer into two words of a protest chant.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright is an adjective meaning total or unqualified, as in an outright lie, matching the complete sense.

clue.text: One river after another in the countryside

definitions.note: an adjective phrase; the answer is the adjective

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian

explanation.surface: Out in the country, one river follows another.
explanation.walkthrough: The first river is just the abbreviation R; the second is a named river, the Ural.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things belonging to country areas as opposed to towns, the same as being out among fields and farms.

clue.text: Counter with publication, clear source of attraction?

blocks.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
short for magazine
to clear a sum is to earn it after deductions, to net it

explanation.surface: A pub counter stocked with magazines is clearly what draws people in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' is the verb, as in to clear a profit, giving NET; the question mark flags that attraction is magnetic, not social.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar magnet is a straight rectangular magnet, literally something that pulls metal towards it through magnetic force.

clue.text: Unreliable type made bankrupt by necessity? About right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word is placed round another

blocks.note: broke means having no money
a need is a necessity
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A shifty character ruined by need, and that is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About right' looks like a casual comment closing the sentence, but it tells you to put the abbreviation for right inside the word for necessity.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken reed is an idiom for a person who cannot be depended upon, from the Bible's image of a weak support.

clue.text: Asian language proves draw by the sound of it

indicators.note: judging by the sound means we listen to a word rather than read it

blocks.note: a tie is a drawn game, where neither side wins

explanation.surface: A language turns out to be a stalemate, or so it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' could be a verb, to sketch or pull, but it is the noun for a level result in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai is the official tongue of Thailand in Southeast Asia, spoken by tens of millions of people.

clue.text: Pinkish-red growths turn up on Chuck, maybe

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from the bottom upward, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: warts are small growths on the skin
Chuck Berry was an early rock and roll guitarist; 'maybe' marks him as one example of the name

explanation.surface: Reddish growths appear on someone called Chuck.
explanation.walkthrough: Chuck looks like a verb, to throw, but it is the first name of the rock pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strawberry is used as a colour name for a pinkish shade of red, after the ripe fruit.

clue.text: Two that stir in a haphazard way, initially

indicators.note: haphazard means random and disordered, so the letters end up in a chance order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people stirring a pot carelessly at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' sits next to 'haphazard' as if it were part of the signal, but it is fodder; all eleven letters of the first three words are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean at the beginning or in the first place, so the adverb and the idiom are interchangeable.

clue.text: Location, we're told, upset Welshman, a tourist

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so a word that sounds like another
in a down clue, to upset is to tip over so that the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: a site is a location
Rees is a common Welsh surname

explanation.surface: A Welshman gets annoyed when a tourist turns up at his place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an emotion but it flips the Welsh name. Rees, like Jones and Evans, is a typically Welsh surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightseer is someone visiting places of interest for pleasure, which is what a tourist does.

clue.text: Insurance policy on rental property, which is found on bed

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for a noun

blocks.note: insurance cover is what a policy provides
a let is a property rented out to a tenant

explanation.surface: A landlord's insurance for a rented flat, including the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a placing word that sits as part of the surface; in the down light the second piece simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A coverlet is a bedspread, the top cloth layer spread over a made bed.

clue.text: Flag shown by old seagoing vessel carrying queen

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a steamer is a steamship, now old-fashioned
R is Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An old ship carrying a queen flies a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: R for Regina, as in royal signatures, slips in after ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow pennant or banner flown from a mast, a kind of flag.

clue.text: One agent had to be redeployed, requiring attention

indicators.note: redeploying moves things into new positions, so the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy is being sent to a new posting and needs looking after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' reads as part of the verb phrase 'had to be', but it belongs to the eleven letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Items on the agenda are listed for discussion or action, so they are matters needing to be dealt with.

clue.text: Doctor is enthralled by fish in Arctic feature

indicators.note: someone enthralled is held captive, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a tuna is a large sea fish
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is captivated by a fish in the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor sits inside the fish, between TUN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless frozen plain found across the far north, a characteristic polar landscape.

clue.text: American with avarice is of the same mind

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
avarice is greed for wealth

explanation.surface: A greedy American finds others thinking just the same.
explanation.walkthrough: A for American is a standard abbreviation, followed by a straight synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are agreed hold a shared opinion, which is exactly being in accord with one another.

clue.text: English archdeacon of a smooth nature

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title given to an archdeacon

explanation.surface: An English archdeacon with a calm temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Church of England an archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable, written Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: Even describes a flat, level surface without bumps, or a steady temperament without ups and downs.

clue.text: Varied stars rejected food around old city

indicators.note: varied means changed around, so the letters take a new order
something rejected is sent back, so the word runs backwards
around means surrounding, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: taken as written
grub is informal for food
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Assorted celebrities turned down the food served round an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: BURG holds O after its first letter; 'old city' looks like the definition, but 'old' is O and only 'city' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Strasbourg is a major city in eastern France, home to the European Parliament, so it is one example.

clue.text: A learner having little vitality gets permit

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the learner driver's plate
feeling low means lacking energy or spirits

explanation.surface: A listless learner driver is granted a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the learner plates on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow is to give permission for something, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: One opposing some Italian timekeeping

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters are a portion of the following words

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone who objects to how Italians keep time.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person who is against something, used informally as a noun for an opponent.

clue.text: Male in Spanish city starts to prefer exquisite entrées, loving covering of fruit

indicators.note: being in a place means being held inside it, so one piece sits within another
starts are beginnings, so each word gives up its opening letter

blocks.note: León is a city in northern Spain
M is the abbreviation for male
opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A man in a Spanish city has refined tastes in starters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loving' looks like an adjective with the definition, but it supplies the last initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon peel is the rind of a citrus fruit, its outer skin, and thus the covering of a fruit.

clue.text: Captain's area on ship missing first raised strip of land

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: the bridge is where the captain commands a ship

explanation.surface: The ship's command post, without its leader, rises up.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIDGE loses its B.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow elevated stretch of ground, such as the crest of a hill range.

clue.text: Man's best friend gets to slip in part of a stand

definitions.note: the definition is any dog; the answer is one breed

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a tier is one level of seating in a stadium stand
to slip is to make an error

explanation.surface: A dog manages to slip into a section of the grandstand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' reads as a physical movement, but here it is the verb to make a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Man's best friend' is a stock phrase for the dog, and the terrier is one popular breed.

clue.text: Irregular method followed by section of a hospital

blocks.note: a way of doing something is a method
a ward is a room or department of a hospital

explanation.surface: An unorthodox treatment procedure is carried out on a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Two straight synonyms placed one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayward means erratic and unpredictable, departing from what is normal or expected behaviour.
